title: Right ankle injury playing basketball
notice: Synthetic conversation written for a software demo. Every name, date, phone number and address is invented. Not medical advice.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Hi there, I'm Doctor Brooks. You must be Tyler?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Yeah, Tyler Nguyen.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Can you give me your date of birth?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: November 22nd, 2001.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: And a phone number we can reach you at?

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Thanks. And your address is 305 Harbourview Lane, Unit 12, Toronto?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Yep, that's it.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: So what happened to your ankle?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I was playing basketball last night and came down from a rebound on my teammate Marcus's foot. My right ankle rolled inward really hard.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Did you hear or feel a pop?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I felt something, kind of a snap, and then it swelled up pretty fast on the outside.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Were you able to walk on it afterwards?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I limped off the court. It hurt, but I could walk to the car, maybe ten or fifteen steps.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: What have you done for it since?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I iced it last night and kept it up on a pillow, and I took 400 milligrams of ibuprofen this morning.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Have you ever hurt this ankle before?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Not this one. I sprained my left ankle about two years ago.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Any numbness or tingling in your foot?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: No, nothing like that.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Okay, let's take a look. There's moderate swelling and some bruising over the outside of your right ankle. Tell me where it hurts. Here, just in front of the ankle bone?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Yeah, right there. That's the worst spot.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: That's over the anterior talofibular ligament. Now I'm pressing on the back edge and the tip of both ankle bones. Any pain?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: No, not really.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: And the base of the fifth metatarsal here, and the navicular on the inside of your foot?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: That's fine.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Your pulses and sensation in the foot are normal. The anterior drawer test shows a bit of laxity compared with the other side. Can you take four steps for me?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: It hurts, but yes, I can do it.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Good. Based on the Ottawa ankle rules, you don't need an X-ray today. There's no bony tenderness, and you can bear weight. This looks like a moderate, grade two sprain of the lateral ligaments.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: How long will I be out of basketball?

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Usually three to four weeks, sometimes a bit longer. For the next few days, keep it elevated, use ice for 15 to 20 minutes at a time, and wear an air-stirrup brace. Crutches are fine for two or three days, but put as much weight on it as you comfortably can.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Can I keep taking the ibuprofen?

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Yes, 400 milligrams every eight hours with food, for up to five days. I'm also referring you to physiotherapy for balance and strengthening exercises, which lowers the chance of spraining it again.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I work at a warehouse. Can I still go in?

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: I'll write a note for modified duties for one week. No heavy lifting and no ladders.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Okay, thanks.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Come back if you can't bear weight at all, if your foot gets numb or cold, or if it's not getting better in a week.
